newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian man fined for keeping koala in freezer.
newsitem.headline: Australian man fined for keeping koala in freezer.

text.p: An amateur Australian taxidermist who kept a dead koala in his freezer for two years has been fined A$1,250 (US$925) for having a threatened species in his possession, a local newspaper reported on Wednesday.

Malcolm Boyle, 31, obtained the koala, a cuddly, slow-moving teddy bear-like animal, from an animal protection officer after it had been killed in a road accident north of Sydney, The Daily Telegragh newspaper said.

The newspaper said a Sydney court on Tuesday heard that Boyle had a fascination for native fauna and his hobby led him to collect "road kills", animals accidentially killed by motorists, and stuff them.

Boyle's collection of stuffed animals included birds such as a sulphur-crested cockatoo, an eastern rosella and a galah, as well as a diamond python and a red-bellied black snake -- all kept in his freezer.
Boyle pleaded guilty to having the koala and other protected animals in his possession, including two live wood ducks, which he said he found in a fox trap.
Boyle's lawyer told the court his client was "a man with a genuine love for native wildlife" who had simply failed to obtain the correct licences to keep the animals.
In fining Boyle, the magistrate said there was no suggestion Boyle had been cruel to the animals.
The newspaper said Boyle left the court accompanied by his dog Mitch and a duck named Daisy.
